title: Lightweight Feature Easel — quick prototype notes
content:
Context:
This is a very rough personal sketch for a tiny feature prototyping surface called the 'Easel' — a friction-light quick-config UI + runtime hook aimed at letting product teams compose and validate hypothesis-driven small LLM behaviors without full infra rollouts. Think: 60–120 minute experiment turnaround.

Why this exists (problem):
- Current small experiments (tweaking instruction templates, response compacting, fidelity knobs) take hours-to-days because of infra changes, long rollout windows, and lots of guardrails.
- Engineers and PMs lose momentum; desk prototypes diverge from production.

Target user personas:
- PM experimenting with tone/verbosity changes across 3 customer cohorts.
- ML engineer validating a new temperature + sampling recipe for a specific intent.
- Solutions engineer testing a size-limited fallback for restricted environments.

Goals / success metrics (first 90 days):
- Time from idea -> measurable signal in prod-like environment < 2 hours (target).
- 25 small experiments run by beta partners across product-hosted-api within 6 weeks.
- Measurable delta captured: conversion metric or automated eval score for the 1st 10 experiments.

Core idea (minimal):
- Tiny UI in Console: create an Easel experiment that wires together: model variant, instruction template, response post-processor, and traffic slice (user property or token-based percentage).
- Runtime binding: a lightweight routing override that applies only to the experiment traffic and can be toggled off instantly. No new model deployments required for most experiments (use model variants).
- Data capture: store prompt/response + evaluation label hooks (automated eval tasks) + basic latency/cost breakdown.

Minimum viable feature set (MVP):
1) Console card where user selects: name, description, model variant, a single instruction template, sample prompt set (paste/upload) and sampling params.
2) Traffic targeting: either API key subset or percent traffic by route.
3) Runtime override path in hosted API: small-match rule table (in-memory) that checks experiment key and routes accordingly.
4) Quick telemetry: per-experiment latency, tokens, error rate, and simple automated score (BLEU-ish / policy pass rate).
5) Rapid rollback button + kill switch.

User stories (examples):
- As a PM I want to run a tone experiment for 5% of web app users so I can measure retention impact without a full rollout. Acceptance: experiment active, 5% traffic tagged, metric pipeline shows comparative retention after 48h.
- As an ML engineer I want to try a low-temp config for a single intent route to reduce hallucinations. Acceptance: route-level binding applied, observability shows top-1 hallucination score dropped on sample eval set.

UX notes / sketches (rough):
- Canvas: name + one-line hypothesis, attach prompt set, choose hypothesis comparator metric, choose target slice, start/stop.
- Quick diff view: sample prompts side-by-side (control vs experiment) with inline annotator.
- Lightweight approvals: owner and one reviewer approval before >10% traffic.

Runtime constraints / safety:
- Must always enforce existing safety/policy filters in mainline path; Easel cannot bypass policy.
- Limit experiment to N concurrent users per org for beta (avoid noisy tenant).
- Auto-expire experiments after 7 days unless renewed.

Telemetry / evaluation pipeline (sketch):
- Plug into existing prompt telemetry. Attach small evaluation harness that runs annotators (automated heuristics + optional human review).
- Emit experiment_id tag on logs/traces and in cost accounting.

Implementation sketch (low fidelity):
- Console: new Easel react component + minimal backend CRUD for experiment entities (owner, config, status).
- Runtime: route-matching middleware: check experiment table keyed by api_key/user_id -> apply override params. Lightweight cache invalidation via pub/sub.
- Storage: experiment configs in central DB; telemetry tagged to experiment id in our existing observability pipeline.

Open questions / risks:
- How to represent complex instruction diffs (templating language needed?). For MVP, keep it literal strings + variable placeholders.
- Cost accounting: experiments may inflate token consumption; need per-experiment metering to bill or annotate.
- Security: experiment configs could be used to exfiltrate — ensure config sanitization and policy enforcement.
- Multi-tenant risk: ensure fair share so a single tenant experiment doesn't consume disproportionate capacity.

Rollout plan (alpha -> beta -> GA):
- Alpha (internal only): Matteo + Lena run 5 internal experiments; refine UI and telemetry.
- Beta (partner teams): open to 3 product teams; gather feedback on hypothesis-editor and evaluation.
- GA: enable self-serve with guardrails, add RBAC and audit logs.

Next steps / immediate TODOs:
- [ ] Spike: build a runtime middleware prototype that accepts an experiment override for route binding (target 1 day).
- [ ] Quick Console mock in figma + share with PM guild (2 days).
- [ ] Draft sign-off checklist for safety & infra limits.
- [ ] Create quick eval harness: small auto-annotation for hallucination and style (3 days).

Notes to self / ideas to explore later:
- Easel as SDK: allow engineers to create experiments via API (not only console).
- Integrate with rollouts for gradual promotion if experiment meets thresholds.
- Shareable experiment templates across org (catalog).

References (internal):
- Slack thread: #easel-ideas (search: easel quick experiment)
- Prior tickets: PROD-512 (prompt telemetry sampling), INFRA-303 (route middleware caching)

Rough backlog (one-liners):
- EAS-1 Console CRUD + model selector
- EAS-2 Runtime override middleware + cache invalidation
- EAS-3 Telemetry tagging + quick scoring job
- EAS-4 Approval flows and limits
- EAS-5 API for programmatic experiment creation

End of scratchpad — keep intentionally messy. Will refine into a 1-pager after the runtime spike.
